payload.name: Preserve explicit enumerated items in memory extraction
payload.description: Use when drafting memory candidates from statements that list multiple distinct attributes, reasons, preferences, or items; ensure every listed element is kept in the memory content.
content: When a source message explicitly enumerates multiple distinct facts (separated by commas/conjunctions), preserve each listed element in the candidate memory content; do not paraphrase away any of them.

Before committing an ADD/UPDATE/MERGE, check the candidate against the source enumeration and append any missing elements; if a memory already exists with a partial list, update it to include the full enumeration.

solves: The diagnosed mechanism is extraction-level loss of enumerated items when a paraphrase collapses a list (e.g., only one of several explicit rewards is kept). This rule repairs that by requiring all enumerated elements to survive into memory candidates. It applies to any future extraction or update of memories about preferences, reasons, outcomes, or other multi-item statements; it does not apply when the source is not an explicit list.
